nodes.rationale: A deliberately small surface — put / get / delete / list plus CAS options — so it fits AWS S3, MinIO, R2, B2, Wasabi and anything else S3-compatible.

nodes.label: CachedSnapshotStore
nodes.rationale: A read-through decorator for hot-path snapshot loading, turning redundant S3 GETs into sub-microsecond cache hits.

nodes.label: keepN pruning
nodes.rationale: Pruning is on by default at keepN 3, so each save keeps only the most recent snapshots per persistenceId and per-pid LISTs stay bounded. keepN:0 disables pruning, and then one pid can accumulate 100K snapshots that every loadLatest LIST has to return.

nodes.label: ObjectStorageSnapshotStore
nodes.rationale: The snapshot store backed by object storage — for cluster-wide shared snapshots that any node can load, encrypted snapshots for compliance, and cheap per-GB storage of read-rarely data. Single-node deployments are faster and simpler on SqliteSnapshotStore.

nodes.label: CAS via ifMatch / ifNoneMatch
nodes.rationale: ifMatch gives compare-and-set writes (a differing ETag fails with ObjectStorageConcurrencyError) and ifNoneMatch:'*' is create-only, which is how ObjectStorageDurableStateStore detects concurrent writers without separate coordination. Some older S3-compatible stores ignore these headers, so the backends throw clearly rather than silently proceeding — test CAS against your provider first.

nodes.label: When object storage is the right backend
nodes.rationale: Cloud-native stacks, shared persistence across cluster nodes without running Cassandra, KMS server-side encryption, and unbounded capacity. It sits between SQLite (simpler for single node) and Cassandra (faster for high-throughput multi-node): 20-50 ms per put versus sub-millisecond on the filesystem backend.
nodes.norm_label: when object storage is the right backend

nodes.label: Journal and snapshot store are independent
nodes.rationale: They can be mixed freely — SQLite journal with object-storage snapshots for local event rate plus shared snapshots for sharded entities, Cassandra plus object storage for both shared, or object storage for everything when S3 is the only storage.
nodes.norm_label: journal and snapshot store are independent

nodes.label: kind-Diskriminator
nodes.rationale: Lowercase, kebab-case for multiple words; the project-wide convention the receiving actor's match dispatches on.

nodes.label: .exhaustive()
nodes.rationale: The compile-time check: adding a kind without its arm fails the build, so a silently dropped message never ships.

nodes.label: .otherwise()
nodes.rationale: Disables the exhaustiveness check, so it is a deliberate choice for actors that handle a subset of a wider message type.

nodes.label: Pattern Matching
nodes.rationale: Three advantages over hand-written if/else ladders: compile-time exhaustiveness, narrowing inside each arm, and readability past five variants.

nodes.label: Try<T>
nodes.rationale: Success<T> | Failure — macht aus einem throw einen Wert, den man weiterreichen kann: in eine Nachricht, ueber ein ask, in eine Zustandsmaschine. Bietet recover, recoverWith, get, toError; trySequence macht aus Try<T>[] ein Try<T[]>.

nodes.label: Either<L, R>
nodes.rationale: Left | Right, right-biased. Reach for it over Try when the failure side is a domain value you want typed - a validation report, a rejection reason - rather than a thrown error.

nodes.label: Option<T>
nodes.rationale: Some<T> | None - preferred over T | null in domain-API returns and long-lived fields because the type forces the empty case to be handled at the point of use rather than remembered. Nullable stays right in three places the framework uses it deliberately: hot-path internal fields where the wrapper would show in a profile, serialization boundaries that round-trip through null, and optional parameters with ergonomic defaults.

nodes.label: Command-vs-Event-Split
nodes.rationale: Events are the durable record replayed on restart while commands are transient, so past tense for events and imperative for commands keeps the conceptual line visible.

nodes.label: Discriminated-Union-Konvention
nodes.rationale: Buys three things: compile-time exhaustiveness, type narrowing inside handlers, and wire-format stability — the wire carries no type identity, so the discriminant must travel inside the payload.

nodes.label: Immutability-Regeln
nodes.rationale: A message can be processed twice (restart replay, reliable redelivery), and cross-process sends hand the receiver a copy — the asymmetry between local and remote mutation is what produces confusing bugs.

nodes.label: Jeder Arm delegiert an einen privaten onXxx-Handler
nodes.rationale: Keeps the matcher a scannable dispatch table with the logic in named handlers; a hard rule in the repo's AGENTS.md, including one-liners and the otherwise fallback.
nodes.norm_label: jeder arm delegiert an einen privaten onxxx-handler

nodes.label: IdempotencyOptions
nodes.rationale: keyPrefix defaults to idem: so multiple wrappers in one Redis do not collide; missingHeader defaults to reject, with pass-through for fleets where only some clients send the header.

nodes.label: RedisCache for multi-pod deployments
nodes.rationale: InMemoryCache is per-pod state, so a retry landing on a different pod re-processes.

nodes.label: Cache loss equals double processing
nodes.rationale: After the TTL the key is forgotten and a delayed retry processes again — pick a TTL longer than any reasonable retry window, 24 hours being typical for payments.

nodes.label: Middleware set (cache / rate limit / idempotency)
nodes.rationale: Each is a handler wrapper composed by nesting at the handler level.

nodes.label: WebSocket handshakes go through app.use
nodes.rationale: A websocket() route is registered as an ordinary GET, so a middleware that answers cancels the handshake and onClientConnected never fires. Two caveats: one that neither answers nor calls next() leaves the client waiting, and a rejection body only reaches the client on runtimes that allow writing to a hijacked upgrade socket — Bun and Node do, Deno does not.

nodes.label: idempotent middleware
nodes.rationale: Enforces at-most-once write processing: the handler runs only on the first request and subsequent requests with the same key replay the stored response, so a network retry cannot double-charge.

nodes.label: In-flight claim returns 409 Conflict
nodes.rationale: The second concurrent request is refused immediately rather than queued. Failing fast instead of holding the connection open for the handler runtime also means there is no cross-pod lock to coordinate — the in-flight marker lives in the same cache as the responses.

nodes.label: InMemoryCache eviction hazards
nodes.rationale: Three silent failure modes even with guarantee-aware eviction: a flood of rate-limit counters evicts records because the policy does not rank guarantees against each other; this middleware own key space is attacker-controlled, so a flood of distinct keys evicts other callers records; and a record is only marked most-recently-used when read, so setIfAbsent leaves a claimed-but-unretried key first to be dropped.

nodes.label: Give each middleware its own cache
nodes.rationale: InMemoryCache is LRU-bounded at 10 000 entries and evicts entries carrying no guarantee first, but it does not rank guarantees against each other — so varying the Idempotency-Key still evicts rate-limit counters and idempotency records once nothing cheaper is left.
nodes.norm_label: give each middleware its own cache

nodes.label: Middleware runs at upgrade time
nodes.rationale: withMiddleware runs once against the HTTP upgrade request, not per message, so auth middleware gates the handshake. Backend-native middleware runs too — Fastify route hooks, Express and Hono app.use — and the framework own guard runs after all of them, so withMiddleware and allowedOrigins always have the last word.

nodes.label: Typed-API (Behaviors als Werte)
nodes.rationale: Eine funktionale Fassade auf der untyped-Engine: Zustand als Parameter statt Felder, pure-funktionales Message-Handling, Sentinels als Transition-Entscheidung, cast-freies Child-Spawning. Ein fehlendes Return ist hier ein Typfehler, in der untyped-Form still okay.

nodes.label: Untyped-API (Actor-Subklasse)
nodes.rationale: Die niedrigere, flexiblere API. Sauberer bei erheblichem mutablem Zustand, bei Lifecycle-Hooks (preStart/postStop/preRestart statt Signal-Events) und beim Interop — die Internas der Cluster-Extensions sind untyped-Klassen, und das leakt gelegentlich an den Naehten.

nodes.label: typedActor(behavior)
nodes.rationale: Die Notluke: gibt eine ActorFactory<T> zurueck fuer Stellen, die eine Actor-Klasse oder Factory nehmen — ein aelterer Einstiegspunkt, ein Spawn mit eigenen ActorOptions, ClusterSingleton.start, der entityActor-Slot der Sharding-Region.

nodes.label: context.setDisplayName(name)
nodes.rationale: The way in for Behaviors actors, which all share one TypedActor class and have no subclass of yours to override.

nodes.label: Wann typed, wann untyped
nodes.rationale: Beide laufen auf demselben Dispatcher, derselben Mailbox, demselben Supervisionsbaum — die Wahl ist Ausdrucksstil, nicht Faehigkeit. Typed fuer State-Machines mit phasenweise verschiedenen Valid-Message-Sets und compiler-gepruefte Transitions; untyped bei grossem mutablem Aggregat oder beim Lernen des Modells.

nodes.label: Initial-Behavior-Fallstricke
nodes.rationale: Behaviors.same als Initial wird wie Behaviors.empty behandelt (stilles No-Op, deutet auf einen Logik-Bug); Behaviors.stopped als Initial stoppt den Actor bereits in preStart.

nodes.label: TypedActor<T>
nodes.rationale: Runtime-Host, der einen Behavior-Wert interpretiert; Actor-Subklasse mit gleicher Mailbox/Dispatcher/Supervisionsbaum. Nicht direkt instanziieren — jeder Restart braucht eine frische Instanz, die nur die Spawn-Helfer erzeugen.

nodes.label: busyTimeoutMs
nodes.rationale: Set explicitly because the drivers disagree (0 ms on bun:sqlite and node:sqlite, 5000 ms on better-sqlite3), which would make the same journal behave differently per runtime. The default is 1000 ms rather than 5000 because the SQLite drivers are synchronous — the wait blocks the event loop, cluster heartbeats included — and the failure detector calls a node unreachable after 2000 ms. A negative value is rejected: SQLite reads it as retry-forever, an unbounded freeze.

nodes.label: SqliteJournal
nodes.rationale: The right default for single-node production: bun:sqlite is built in on Bun, better-sqlite3 is a single optional peer on Node, node:sqlite covers Deno.

nodes.label: WAL mode
nodes.rationale: Recommended for production — readers do not block the writer, commits are sequential, crash recovery is simpler. Default off to match SQLite's own defaults.

nodes.label: No transactions — by transport, not by choice
nodes.rationale: D1's HTTP API exposes one statement per request: no BEGIN and no parameterized batch. The journal stays correct because concurrency never depended on the transaction — appends are contiguous from the head, so two writers try the same first sequence number and the loser fails on its first insert. The cost is that a connection failure mid multi-event append leaves the already-written events written.
nodes.norm_label: no transactions — by transport, not by choice

nodes.label: Remote databases only
nodes.rationale: A file: or :memory: URL is rejected at construction with a pointer to SqliteJournal, rather than letting the driver's HTTP entry point raise URL_SCHEME_NOT_SUPPORTED on the first append.

nodes.label: No transactions required
nodes.rationale: Multi-document transactions would need a replica set, so the backend deliberately avoids them and works on a standalone mongod. It is sound rather than lucky: appends are contiguous from the head, so the losing writer's insertMany fails on its very first document and ordered:true stops the batch there. A dropped connection mid-batch can still persist a prefix.

nodes.label: BEGIN IMMEDIATE head re-read
nodes.rationale: Locally the journal re-reads the head sequence inside a BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction and raises JournalConcurrencyError before attempting any insert — the primary key is only a backstop here. The HTTP-fronted backends have no such transaction and must let the write hit (persistence_id, sequence_nr) instead: same tables, weaker guarantee.

nodes.label: Do not share a SQLite file across processes
nodes.rationale: SQLite supports concurrent processes, but the framework's prepared statements and in-process JournalEventBus do not know about another process's writes, so push-based queries miss cross-process events. Network filesystems break locking outright.
nodes.norm_label: do not share a sqlite file across processes

nodes.label: SQLite driver auto-detection
nodes.rationale: Bun to bun:sqlite, Node to better-sqlite3 when installed else node:sqlite, Deno to node:sqlite — every supported runtime has a driver that needs no install. The concrete driver classes are not public API; the driver slot is an internal seam the framework's own tests use.

nodes.label: Backend matrix
nodes.rationale: Twelve rows crossing journal / durable state / snapshot store / indexed tag query / runtimes. CockroachDB and YugabyteDB are not separate backends but Postgres-wire servers the Postgres stores serve unchanged; Cassandra has no durable-state store and object storage has no journal. 'Indexed tag query' means currentEventsByTag can be pushed down to storage — the others scan and refine in memory, correct either way but bounded in cost only where there is an index.

nodes.label: Projections / ProjectionActor
nodes.rationale: Decouples writes from reads: the projection consumes tagged events in order and persists its own offset so a restart resumes correctly. A throwing handler blocks every event behind it because the cursor only advances on success, which recoveryStrategy bounds — retry with backoff then stop, or skip to the dead-letter stream.

nodes.label: InMemoryQuery
nodes.rationale: The reference implementation, not the in-memory-only one: it works against ANY Journal, so a backend without its own query class can still run projections. What is lost is the index, and only on the by-tag methods — currentEventsByTag lists every persistence id, replays each from sequence 1 and filters in process, per call. Correct at any volume, fast only at small ones, and nothing warns you.

nodes.label: PersistenceQuery
nodes.rationale: The read-side API over the journal in two flavours: current* resolves once with a materialized array, events* is a live AsyncIterable that polls until the consumer stops. The interface is identical across implementations — construct the one for your backend and pass it the journal instance, not a connection string.

nodes.label: Data dies with the process
nodes.rationale: The journal is a Map in process memory: restart means total data loss, it is not shared across processes, and it grows unbounded until delete is called. Legitimate only for tests, dev and throwaway demos.

nodes.label: Reference semantics for every journal
nodes.rationale: InMemoryJournal is the reference implementation every other journal must match — append-only, monotonic sequence numbers, exact-once delivery to subscribers, concurrency check on the expected sequence. Swapping to a real journal is one line because the Journal interface is unchanged.

nodes.label: A compacted event leaves the tag index too
nodes.rationale: delete is specified against the read side as well: once a prefix is compacted, currentEventsByTag stops returning it. Backends whose index sits on the event record get that for free; those with a separate structure delete from it in the same call and BEFORE the events, so a crash mid-delete cannot strand rows whose keys are no longer reconstructible. Worth knowing when writing your own journal — read and highestSeq look perfectly correct while a forgotten index keeps serving deleted events.
nodes.norm_label: a compacted event leaves the tag index too

nodes.label: SQLite dialect schema
nodes.rationale: Five tables (events, events_tags, events_meta, snapshots, durable_state) created with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, shared verbatim with libSQL/Turso and Cloudflare D1 — the same DDL runs on all three, which is what lets a database move between them without a migration.

nodes.label: Interactive-transaction append
nodes.rationale: The append reads the head and inserts inside one interactive transaction; the primary key translates SQLITE_CONSTRAINT into JournalConcurrencyError as a backstop, so the guarantee holds even when the transport cannot give strict isolation. Write transactions hold the server's write lock for roughly five seconds.

nodes.label: No native binding
nodes.rationale: The @libsql/client driver speaks HTTP and WebSocket, so it runs on every supported runtime and inside edge sandboxes that cannot load native addons — the only SQLite-flavoured backend that works on Deno and at the edge.

nodes.label: SQLite schema compatibility
nodes.rationale: The tables and statements are identical to the local SQLite backend (and Cloudflare D1), so a database moves between a local file and Turso in either direction without a migration.

nodes.label: Dual-table tag design
nodes.rationale: events.tags keeps the legacy CSV column for back-compat while tag queries read the indexed events_tags table instead of scanning every row. Both are written in the same transaction, so they cannot drift apart.

nodes.label: comparison benchmark group
nodes.rationale: The one directory run-all.ts does not discover: its targets are third-party code that must not enter the shipped dependency closure, bun audit's surface, or bun run bench on a clean clone.

nodes.label: worker benchmark group
nodes.rationale: Bun Workers give true multi-core parallelism, unlike a router pool inside one ActorSystem which only gives in-flight concurrency.

nodes.label: highResNow runtime-neutral timer
nodes.rationale: Bun.nanoseconds() on Bun, performance.now() x 1e6 elsewhere, so one harness measures identically on all three runtimes.

nodes.label: Bordered benchmark result table
nodes.rationale: Memory is printed with an explicit sign and tinted above 10 MB / 100 MB so leaky cases stand out; colours honour NO_COLOR and drop when stdout is not a TTY.

nodes.label: run-all.ts discovery driver
nodes.rationale: Spawns every discovered benchmark file in its own subprocess and exits non-zero if any suite failed, so one broken benchmark neither hides the rest nor passes CI.

nodes.label: ACTOR_TS_BENCH_SMOKE smoke mode
nodes.rationale: Collapses every case to one unwarmed iteration; the numbers are meaningless by design and the point is proving each suite still executes against the current src/ API.

nodes.label: typecheck:bench benchmarks-only compile
nodes.rationale: The build tsconfig excludes benchmarks/, so a src/ change that orphaned a benchmark used to be invisible; the typecheck is stricter than smoke because a missing barrel export is a compile error even when the binding is never called.

nodes.label: Underscore-prefixed helper files
nodes.rationale: Files named _x.ts are used BY benchmarks and skipped by the discovery driver, so a bootstrap file is never run as a suite.

nodes.label: Heaviest handlers list
nodes.rationale: Leaf frames ranked by self time, tinted with the error colour when the frame recorded failures.

nodes.label: State diff at a sequence number
nodes.rationale: Reports events folded, whether a snapshot was the starting point, and the fold source; unchanged fields are hidden unless asked for, and truncation for transport is stated.
nodes.norm_label: state diff at a sequence number

nodes.label: Time travel panel
nodes.rationale: Reads a persistence journal and reconstructs state at any point; read-only by design, nothing here writes to a journal or to a live actor.

nodes.label: Explain-Plan
nodes.rationale: Ein Ring der letzten Nachrichtenverarbeitungen eines Actors, aus dem Panel eingeschaltet — keine Codeaenderung, kein Neustart. Beantwortet "was macht dieser Actor gerade", waehrend er sich danebenbenimmt.

nodes.label: Spalten des Explain-Plans
nodes.rationale: seq (Luecke = der Ring hat ueberschrieben), time, message, sender, waited und handled; der Punkt je Zeile traegt das Ergebnis — gruen, amber fuer gestasht, rot fuer einen Handler, der geworfen hat.

nodes.label: Explain-Plan aus Code
nodes.rationale: Derselbe Recorder liegt auf dem ActorContext: enableExplainPlan({ capacity }), explainPlan() liefert aelteste-zuerst, disableExplainPlan() stoppt und verwirft.

nodes.label: Tap-Requests
nodes.rationale: Pull-Operationen, benannt nach ihrem Panel: explain.*, journal.*, replay.*, profiler.*, stats.history, tracing.buffer. Sie werden ausserhalb der Mailbox des Taps beantwortet, damit ein langsamer Journal-Read keine anderen Tabs blockiert; eine Methode ohne Handler antwortet mit unavailable.

nodes.label: Der Diff
nodes.rationale: Gezeigt wird die Aenderung zwischen dem gewaehlten Punkt und dem davor, weil "was hat dieses Event getan" meist die Frage ist. Feldpfade sind gepunktet, unveraenderte Felder liegen hinter einem Schalter, der volle Zustand ist einen Klick entfernt.

nodes.label: withReplayFolds
nodes.rationale: Registriert match/initialState/fold fuer IDs, deren Actor nicht laeuft — eine abgeschlossene Saga, eine passivierte Entity, ein nachtraeglich untersuchtes Journal. withReplayAutoCapture(false) schaltet das Borgen ganz ab.

nodes.label: CPU profiling mode
nodes.rationale: Hands back a standard V8 cpuprofile that the panel deliberately does not render - Chrome DevTools does that better than a bundled UI would. It needs node:inspector, so the panel asks before offering the mode and greys it out with the reason rather than failing at start.

nodes.label: Heaviest handlers ranking
nodes.rationale: Ranks the leaves by their own time - the shortest route from something is slow to this handler is slow.

nodes.label: Speedscope export
nodes.rationale: Wallclock produces speedscope JSON that speedscope.app opens unchanged - useful for keeping a profile alongside a bug report or comparing two runs.

nodes.label: Wallclock profiling mode
nodes.rationale: Groups by actor path then message type, always available. The timings are the framework own per-message measurements, so the profile measures what the actor system actually did rather than what a sampler happened to catch.

nodes.label: One runtime, named (Bun)
nodes.rationale: Fairness rule 5, and a limitation rather than a preference: the shared harness pulls in src/ for highResNow, whose .js suffixes and two enums Node's strip-only TypeScript mode cannot load, so running the neighbours on Node would mean not running them through the same harness.

nodes.label: Comparative, not absolute numbers
nodes.rationale: Single-machine, single-JIT measurements say nothing about a production cluster; treat them as a lower bound on latency and an upper bound on throughput, useful for detecting regressions between commits, not as marketing material.

nodes.label: CPU mode disabled with the reason in the label
nodes.rationale: On Bun the inspector module imports fine and throws only when a session is constructed, so without asking first the reader meets a runtime's internal error message instead of an explanation. V8 profiles are also not rendered here: download and open the .cpuprofile in Chrome DevTools, which does it better.
nodes.norm_label: cpu mode disabled with the reason in the label

nodes.label: Replay folds and the onEvent requirement
nodes.rationale: Events can be read without a fold, but turning them back into state needs onEvent, which lives in the actor class; either start the actor that owns the id or register a fold in DevToolsOptions.replayFolds. An auto-captured fold is accurate as long as it is pure, which the framework requires anyway.
nodes.norm_label: replay folds and the onevent requirement

nodes.label: Kosten des Explain-Plans
nodes.rationale: Ein Zeitstempel beim Einreihen und ein Ring-Eintrag fester Groesse pro Nachricht; der Ring waechst nie ueber seine Kapazitaet, und das Panel deckelt eine angeforderte Kapazitaet bei 10 000 — es ist eine Debug-Hilfe, kein Log. Ein Ring, der weiterlaeuft, weil ein Tab geschlossen wurde, waere ein Leck.

nodes.label: Mailbox-Wartezeit schliesst den Stash ein
nodes.rationale: Eine gestashte Nachricht behaelt beim Wiedereinspielen ihren urspruenglichen Zeitstempel — vier Sekunden im Stash sind vier Sekunden Wartezeit. Eine Nachricht, die beim Einschalten schon in der Queue lag, zeigt statt einer erfundenen Null ein Strich.

nodes.label: Pro Actor und opt-in
nodes.rationale: Jede Nachricht auf jedem Actor aufzuzeichnen kostete mehr als viele der gemessenen Handler selbst. Die Frage stellt sich immer fuer einen Actor, also wird auch nur fuer einen bezahlt — ein Actor ohne Plan laeuft wie vorher, bis auf einen Null-Check auf dem Dispatch-Pfad.

nodes.label: CPU-Modus
nodes.rationale: Liefert ein normales V8-.cpuprofile, das das Panel bewusst nicht rendert — die Chrome DevTools koennen das besser. Es braucht node:inspector, deshalb fragt das Panel die Faehigkeit vorab ab und graut die Option mit Begruendung aus, statt erst beim Start zu scheitern.

nodes.label: Kosten des Profilers
nodes.rationale: Genau ein Observer auf dem Dispatch-Pfad fuer die Dauer einer Session, danach inklusive Wiederherstellung dessen, was vorher dort war; ausserhalb einer Session ein Null-Check pro Nachricht. durationMs ist bei zehn Minuten gedeckelt — ein Profiler ist eine Messung, kein Monitoring-Agent.

nodes.label: Nur eine Session gleichzeitig
nodes.rationale: Zwei ueberlappende Profile saehen je einen Teil des Bildes und keines waere richtig. Eine Session, die weiterlaeuft, weil ein Tab geschlossen wurde, wird beim Detachen gestoppt — der Hook ueberlebt nie das, was ihn angefordert hat.

nodes.label: Read-only, per Konstruktion
nodes.rationale: Nichts in diesem Panel schreibt in ein Journal, einen Snapshot-Store oder einen lebenden Actor: "Wie sah das aus?" ist eine Frage, und sie zu beantworten darf die Antwort nicht veraendern.

nodes.label: Woher der Fold kommt
nodes.rationale: Events zurueck in Zustand zu verwandeln verlangt onEvent, das in der Actor-Klasse lebt und sich nicht aus gespeicherten Daten rekonstruieren laesst. auto-captured borgt es vom laufenden Actor, registered kommt aus DevToolsOptions; eine explizite Registrierung schlaegt Auto-Capture, weil sie eine bewusste Aussage ist. Trifft keines zu, sagt das Panel das und laesst das Event-Log weiterlaufen.

nodes.label: Derselbe Fold wie im Actor
nodes.rationale: Rekonstruiert wird mit replayState — exakt der Funktion, die auch die PersistentActor-Recovery aufruft, inklusive Snapshot-Fast-Path und Integritaetspruefungen. Ein Debugger mit leicht anderem Replay duerfte von dem abweichen, was der Actor tatsaechlich recovert. Folge: ein Sprung weit zurueck ist so guenstig wie eine Recovery.

nodes.label: Grenzen und Sicherheit
nodes.rationale: Grosse Werte werden fuer den Transport gekuerzt (und das Panel sagt es) — ein Debugger darf nicht der Grund sein, aus dem ein System umfaellt; Event-Seiten sind bei 200/2 000 gedeckelt. Das Panel legt rohe persistierte Events offen und ist damit das erste, das man ausserhalb einer Entwicklungsmaschine abschaltet.

nodes.label: Aggregated flame graph
nodes.rationale: This flame graph has no clock: identical stacks are summed, so a handler called ten thousand times appears once, as wide as the time it consumed in total. Use the tracing panel when you care about a single request and this one when you care about the whole system.

nodes.label: One profiling session at a time
nodes.rationale: Two overlapping profiles would each see part of the picture and neither would be right. A session left running because a browser tab closed is stopped when DevTools detaches, so the hook never outlives the thing that asked for it, and sessions can auto-stop after a duration capped at ten minutes because a profiler is a measurement, not a monitoring agent.
nodes.norm_label: one profiling session at a time

nodes.label: Environment-Substitution ${?ENV} / ${ENV}
nodes.rationale: Der Weg, Credentials aus application.conf herauszuhalten und die Bind-Adresse komplett aus dem Code zu ziehen.

nodes.label: Drei Auflösungsschichten (Code > Nutzer-Config > Reference)
nodes.rationale: Jede Schicht überlagert die vorherige, pro Feld statt pro Block; ein undefined im Code bedeutet 'nicht gesetzt' und fällt durch.

nodes.label: Präzedenz: explizite Optionen > application.conf > reference.conf
nodes.rationale: Pro Feld statt pro Block; setzt du eine Failure-Detector-Schwelle im Code, kommen die anderen weiterhin aus der Config-Datei.

nodes.label: Wo der eingebaute Default steht
nodes.rationale: Options-Defaults stehen neben ihrem Feld in der passenden XOptions.ts, alles andere in einer Constants.ts (src/<subsystem>/ oder src/util/) — ein reference.conf-Blatt und sein Code-Fallback sind damit immer genau zwei Dateien, und die zweite ist nach der ersten benannt.

nodes.label: include-Direktiven werden abgelehnt
nodes.rationale: Ein aufgelöstes include überließe demjenigen, der die Config schreibt, die Wahl der gelesenen Pfade — relativ zu einer Wurzel, die der Parser nicht kennen kann. Zusammenführen im Code (Config.parseFile + merge) belässt die Wahl beim Aufrufer; der Parser zitiert Zeile und Ziel.

nodes.label: AllForOneStrategy
nodes.rationale: Reach for it only when the children states are explicitly coupled — a producer/consumer pair over an internal channel, actors that must restart together.

nodes.label: defaultStrategy / stoppingStrategy / escalatingStrategy
nodes.rationale: defaultStrategy restarts everything capped at 10 per minute — the cap exists precisely to break the infinite restart loop of a child that crashes on every message.

nodes.label: DeathPactError
nodes.rationale: There is no automatic death pact in actor-ts — the runtime never raises it. A death pact is a policy about this watcher, and onReceive returns void, so the cell cannot tell an ignored Terminated from a handled one; leaving the throw to the user is the point rather than a gap.

nodes.label: exhaustive() without a Terminated arm restarts the watcher
nodes.rationale: ts-pattern throws on the unmatched Terminated, which is an ordinary failure and goes through supervision — under the default strategy a death that does not concern the watcher becomes a restart loop.
nodes.norm_label: exhaustive() without a terminated arm restarts the watcher

nodes.label: maxRetries + withinTimeRangeMs
nodes.rationale: Past the bound the supervisor stops the affected children instead of restarting. The parent-side counter is inclusive of the failure that trips it, so maxRetries 10 tolerates eleven restarts before the twelfth failure stops the child.

nodes.label: CompressionConfig
nodes.rationale: Three modes only — none, gzip, zstd; there is deliberately no brotli or deflate. Level is algorithm-specific and out-of-range values are clamped.

nodes.label: compression() per-actor hook
nodes.rationale: Overrides the store-level default per actor class — none for tiny state, high-level zstd for large text-heavy state. Returning undefined falls back to the store default; the framework calls it on each persist.

nodes.label: integrity() per-actor hook
nodes.rationale: The third hook alongside compression() and encryption(): signs the stored body with HMAC-SHA256 so tamper-in-place is detected at read, worthwhile even for data that is not secret. Configuring it makes the tag mandatory on read.

nodes.label: Decompression cap (bomb protection)
nodes.rationale: Read output is bounded to 512 MiB by default so a few KB inflating to many GB cannot exhaust memory during recovery. gzip and zstd hand the bound to the decoder via zlib's maxOutputLength, refusing an over-cap body before its output is allocated; the two paths that cannot take the option (Bun's zstdDecompressSync and the fzstd fallback) only assert the decoded size afterwards, so there the bound is a correctness check rather than bomb protection. Raise it with withMaxDecompressedBytes.

nodes.label: Level is an encoder-only setting
nodes.rationale: The manifest records the algorithm, not the level, and gzip and zstd frames are self-describing — so changing the configured level needs no migration and old and new bodies mix freely.

nodes.label: Only the object-storage stores read these hooks
nodes.rationale: Ten of the eleven snapshot stores and nine of the ten durable-state stores accept PersistenceOptions and never look at it (#960). On SQLite, Postgres, Cassandra, Mongo, DynamoDB and the in-memory reference store an integrity(), encryption() or compression() override buys nothing and raises no error — the directive is dropped on the floor. Verify the control against the store you actually run.
nodes.norm_label: only the object-storage stores read these hooks

nodes.label: Reads follow the manifest, not the current override
nodes.rationale: Decoding uses the self-describing ATS1 manifest carried in the body, so an object encrypted under pciKeyRing is decrypted via pciKeyRing whether or not the actor's current encryption() says so — rotating an actor's policy therefore does not break old data as long as the keys and algorithms are still available.
nodes.norm_label: reads follow the manifest, not the current override

nodes.label: distributed_data_gossip_skipped_keys_total
nodes.rationale: Ein einzelner Key, dessen Kodierung das Budget ueberschreitet, ist unteilbar - er wird uebersprungen, ratenbegrenzt gewarnt und gezaehlt: dieser Key konvergiert nicht.

nodes.label: gossipInterval
nodes.rationale: Default 1 s als Balance zwischen Propagationsgeschwindigkeit und Bandbreite; auch ueber actor-ts.distributed-data.gossip-interval setzbar, Builder gewinnt.

nodes.label: max-gossip-bytes
nodes.rationale: Default 1 MiB, immer auf remote.max-frame-bytes heruntergeschnitten. Ohne Budget erzeugte ein grosser Store ein Frame jenseits des Wire-Caps, das der Empfaenger schon am 4-Byte-Laengenpraefix ablehnt und dabei die Verbindung verwirft - ueber die auch Heartbeats, Membership-Gossip und jedes tell laufen.

nodes.label: dd.subscribe
nodes.rationale: Feuert synchron nach jedem Merge, der den lokalen Wert aendert (Deep-Equal ueber toJSON); Subscriptions sind lokal, idempotente Updates feuern nicht.

nodes.label: preRestart / postRestart
nodes.rationale: preStart laeuft einmal auf dem brandneuen Actor, postRestart bei jedem Restart; der Default macht sie aequivalent. Separat ueberschreiben, wenn ein Restart anderes Verhalten braucht als der erste Start.

nodes.label: stopChildrenOnRestart()
nodes.rationale: Kinder werden gestoppt, weil sonst ein Actor, der in preStart ein benanntes Kind spawnt, beim ersten Restart in 'Child name is not unique' lief. Wer aussteigt, muss preStart idempotent halten und das ueberlebende Kind aus der Zelle uebernehmen (context.child), nie aus einem Instanzfeld. Eigener Hook statt preRestart-Override, weil auf den Abbau gewartet werden muss.

nodes.label: Anti-Entropy-Gossip-Topologie
nodes.rationale: All-to-all ueber die Zeit, O(N) pro Node pro Runde; ab 50+ Nodes relevant, andere Topologien sind aktuell nicht konfigurierbar.

nodes.label: Per-Key-CRDT-Merge
nodes.rationale: Idempotent und kommutativ - deshalb ist das Zuschneiden eines Frames sicher: ein fehlender Key heisst keine Information, nicht geloescht; ein Key spaeter oder doppelt aendert nur wann, nicht wohin der Cluster konvergiert.

nodes.label: Eventual Convergence
nodes.rationale: Gossip ueberbrueckt keine Partitionen - CRDTs garantieren eventual convergence, nicht Echtzeit-Zustellung; Lesepfade sollten mit veralteten Daten funktionieren.

nodes.label: Gossip-Replikation
nodes.rationale: Periodisches Full-State-Gossip an einen zufaelligen Peer; Writes propagieren eventually (typisch 1-2 Runden). Lokale Writes sind sofort, Gossip ist nur fuer die Propagation.

nodes.label: MemberRemoved ist ein No-op fuer DistributedData
nodes.rationale: Es gibt keinen Zustand pro Peer - kein Version Vector, keine Empfangs-Historie; jeder Tick waehlt aus den aktuellen Up-Members, ein ausgeschiedener Node ist damit einfach kein Ziel mehr.
nodes.norm_label: memberremoved ist ein no-op fuer distributeddata

nodes.label: Zufaellige Peer-Auswahl pro Runde
nodes.rationale: Round-Robin waere vorhersagbarer, erzeugt aber synchronisierte Wellen; ein zufaelliger Peer pro Tick verteilt die Last und konvergiert typisch in O(log N) Runden - Wahrscheinlichkeit (1 - 1/N)^K, dass ein Peer ein Update nach K Runden nicht hat.

nodes.label: CRDT-Tombstones
nodes.rationale: Werden nie garbage-collected, damit veraltetes Gossip einen entfernten Key nicht wiederauferstehen laesst; ueber einen langlebigen Store mit Churn ist die Akkumulation der praktische Kostenpunkt.

nodes.label: Klassenform und Factory-Form
nodes.rationale: An instance is rejected because the actor is rebuilt on every restart — reusing one means inheriting the broken state of the failed run, the opposite of let-it-crash; a closure returning a captured instance defeats it in a way the type system cannot catch.

nodes.label: Restart-Semantik (Zustandsverlust)
nodes.rationale: Instanzfelder sind verloren, die Mailbox bleibt, die fehlgeschlagene Nachricht wird verworfen. Restart bewahrt bewusst KEINEN In-Memory-Zustand - 'let it crash' vertraut dem Recovery-Pfad mehr als dem Per-Message-Guard; wer Zustand braucht, persistiert ihn (PersistentActor, DistributedData) oder waehlt Resume.

nodes.label: Dead Letter fuer uebersprungene Events
nodes.rationale: Publishen ist standardmaessig alles, was passiert - ohne Abonnent ist das Event weg. Die Dead-Letter-Queue bewahrt sie stattdessen auf, filterbar nach der ueberspringenden Projektion.

nodes.label: onFailure-Hook
nodes.rationale: Das strukturierte Signal fuer Alerting. Ein Hook, der selbst wirft, wird geloggt und verschluckt - ein kaputter Reporter darf die Projektion nicht mitreissen.

nodes.label: Projektions-Metriken (stalled / failures_total / events_skipped_total)
nodes.rationale: Logs geben eine Error-Zeile beim Beginn und beim Ende einer Fehlerserie; die Retries dazwischen gehen nach debug, sodass eine tagelang festhaengende Projektion zwei Error-Zeilen kostet statt einer pro Poll.

nodes.label: recoveryStrategy (retry-and-fail / retry-and-skip / fail / skip)
nodes.rationale: Default retry-and-fail: eine still veraltete View ist schlimmer als eine sichtbar gestoppte. Retries sind verzoegert und verdoppeln sich bis maxRetryBackoffMs.

nodes.label: `fail` stoppt den Actor, statt den Fehler entkommen zu lassen
nodes.rationale: Der Supervisor der Projektions-Gruppe startet seine Kinder neu; ein entkommender Fehler wuerde denselben Cursor neu laden und am selben Event scheitern - eine Restart-Schleife, die lauter und kein bisschen nuetzlicher ist. Eine gestoppte Projektion behaelt ihren Cursor.
nodes.norm_label: `fail` stoppt den actor, statt den fehler entkommen zu lassen

nodes.label: Ein fehlschlagender Handler blockiert den Kopf der Warteschlange
nodes.rationale: Der Cursor rueckt erst vor, nachdem handle zurueckgekehrt ist - jedes spaetere Event wartet hinter dem fehlgeschlagenen. recoveryStrategy entscheidet, wie lange das so bleibt.
nodes.norm_label: ein fehlschlagender handler blockiert den kopf der warteschlange

nodes.label: Roadmap-Items (additiv)
nodes.rationale: OTel-Auto-Instrumentation-Politur, mehr Cluster-Transports (WebSocket-Bridge, QUIC), Sharding Rebalance v2, mehr CRDT-Typen. Keines davon bricht bestehenden Code.

nodes.label: Status-Ueberblick (stabil vs. experimentell)
nodes.rationale: Stabil: Core Actor-Modell, Supervision, Mailboxes/Dispatchers, Cluster-Membership, Sharding, Singleton, DistributedPubSub, DistributedData, PersistentActor, Snapshot Stores, Migration Adapters, HTTP-Route-DSL, Broker-Actors, Lease-Interface. Experimentell: Replicated Event Sourcing, Worker Mesh, ProducerController/ConsumerController.

nodes.label: Versionspolitik (SemVer pre-1.0)
nodes.rationale: Patch 0.x.Y = Bugfixes; Minor 0.X.0 = neue Features, koennen Breaking Changes enthalten; 1.0.0 = API-Stabilisierungs-Commitment. Nach 1.0 striktes SemVer.

nodes.label: Deprecation-Politik (harter Schnitt)
nodes.rationale: Vor 1.0 gibt es keinen garantierten Deprecation-Zyklus: die alte API ist in genau der Version weg, die die neue einfuehrt. Dafuer kennzeichnet das CHANGELOG jeden Breaking Change mit einem BREAKING-Marker und einer Migrationsnotiz, und Beispiele und Doku werden in derselben Aenderung umgestellt. Nach 1.0 wird daraus ein echter Zyklus ueber mindestens eine ganze Major-Version.

nodes.label: Was experimentell bedeutet
nodes.rationale: Signaturen koennen sich aendern, Verhalten auf nicht-offensichtliche Weise, Performance ist nicht optimiert. Produktionseinsatz ist OK, aber Code muss bei Minor-Bumps aktualisiert werden; tief experimentelle Features sagen das explizit auf ihrer Seite.

nodes.label: Was stabil bedeutet
nodes.rationale: Erlaubt bleiben additive Aenderungen: optionale Parameter, neue Config-Sub-Keys, neue Return-Type-Felder. NICHT stabil sind Umbenennungen von Methoden oder Klassen und das Entfernen von Funktionalitaet.

nodes.label: register (ID-Lookup) und bind (Routing)
nodes.rationale: bind nimmt eine numerische ID, also muss zuerst registriert werden; das Mapping läuft über den Konstruktor (instanceof), Plain-Objekte fallen auf den Default zurück und Subklassen matchen die Bindung des Parents.

nodes.label: SerializationExtension (Registry)
nodes.rationale: Mappt Klassen über bind auf Serializer und schlägt beim ext.encode den gebundenen Serializer nach; IDs 1-99 sind für die eingebauten reserviert.

nodes.label: setDefault ändert nur den Extension-Default
nodes.rationale: Es rüstet CBOR nicht auf den Cluster-Wire oder die Persistenz-Stores um: beide schreiben den getaggten JSON-Tree und ziehen die Registry nicht heran. Der unterstützte Weg in einen Store ist dessen withSerializer(...); für den Wire gibt es das noch nicht (#450).

nodes.label: Serializer-IDs ≥ 100 sind ein Wire-Vertrag
nodes.rationale: 1-99 gehören den eingebauten (JSON = 1, CBOR = 2), der Konstruktor lehnt Kleineres ab; die ID steckt in jeder gespeicherten Zeile — ändert man sie, hören alte Zeilen auf zu dekodieren.

nodes.label: Die Registry-Bindings werden nirgends konsultiert (#450)
nodes.rationale: encodeFrame ruft die Tree-Walker direkt auf; der einklinkbare Serializer wird auf der Leitung nicht konsultiert, und Persistenz-Stores erreicht ein eigener Serializer nur über withSerializer(...). Das Wiring ist offen als #450.

nodes.label: Unverified against real D1
nodes.rationale: No D1 container image exists and locally it lives only inside wrangler/Miniflare, so the transport layer (auth, response envelope, rate limits, error reporting) has no live integration suite — only the shared SQL, the contract suite against a fake, and unit tests against a stubbed fetch.

nodes.label: Zero-dependency REST transport
nodes.rationale: D1 has no Node SDK outside a Worker, so the backend speaks the REST API with the framework's own HttpClient. It is the only backend that adds nothing to the dependency tree, at the cost of one HTTPS round-trip per statement.

nodes.label: MERGE … WITH (HOLDLOCK) upsert
nodes.rationale: Without the hint, two concurrent merges can both take the NOT MATCHED branch and one fails on the primary key.

nodes.label: Nonclustered tags primary key
nodes.rationale: NVARCHAR(n) counts 2n bytes toward an index key, so (tag, timestamp, persistence_id, sequence_nr) needs 1036 bytes — past SQL Server's 900-byte clustered limit but inside the 1700-byte nonclustered one. That is why the key is nonclustered, why ids and tags are capped at 255 characters, and why SQL Server 2016 or later is required.

nodes.label: A binary wire format per event version
nodes.norm_label: a binary wire format per event version

nodes.label: serializerId mismatch is loud, not silent
nodes.norm_label: serializerid mismatch is loud, not silent

nodes.label: Methoden-Kombinatoren
nodes.rationale: DELETE heisst del, weil delete ein JS-Schluesselwort ist.

nodes.label: concat(...routes)
nodes.rationale: The OR-combinator for multiple routes at the same level.

nodes.label: path(segment, child)
nodes.rationale: Prepends a static segment to every child route and composes; segments with slashes flatten, so path('api/v1', x) equals path('api', path('v1', x)).

nodes.label: First-Match-Wins in concat
nodes.rationale: concat ist ein OR-Kombinator mit First-Match-Semantik; zwei Routen, die denselben Request matchen, fuehren dazu, dass nur die erste laeuft — das Framework warnt nicht davor.

nodes.label: First-match-wins matching
nodes.rationale: concat is OR with first-match semantics, so two routes that pattern-match the same request leave only the first reachable. The framework does not warn about this - reviewing the routing tree is the only check.

nodes.label: Debugging: warum ein Actor keine Nachrichten empfängt
nodes.rationale: Gestoppter Ref (deadLetters), volle Mailbox mit reject-Overflow (MailboxFullError am Sender), noch laufende Recovery, oder fehlgeschlagene Recovery — bei verschlucktem onRecoveryFailure ist die Logzeile 'recovery failed and onRecoveryFailure returned without rethrowing'.
nodes.norm_label: debugging: warum ein actor keine nachrichten empfangt

nodes.label: Debugging: warum Events nicht abgespielt werden
nodes.rationale: Geänderte persistenceId, falsches Journal-Plugin, oder ein Snapshot mit höherer seqNr als das Journal — den lehnt das Framework als Korruptions-Schutz ab.
nodes.norm_label: debugging: warum events nicht abgespielt werden

nodes.label: Plugin-Keys sind voll qualifizierte Pfade
nodes.rationale: Der Plugin-Key zeigt auf den Config-Abschnitt, in dem die Settings dieses Plugins leben; Kurznamen wie "sqlite" werden nicht aufgelöst.

nodes.label: Was bewusst fehlt (Plugin-Subtrees und Nicht-Werte)
nodes.rationale: Defaults für optionale Peers auszuliefern hieße, Konfiguration für ein womöglich gar nicht installiertes Paket auszuliefern; und eine Config-Datei kann keine Klasse und keine Closure ausdrücken — Entity-Actor, Extraktoren, Allocation Strategies, Leases, Transports und Downing Provider bleiben im Code.

nodes.label: Per-Instanz-Cache-Pfade sind nicht auflistbar
nodes.rationale: Der Name gehört der Anwendung (actor-ts.cache.<name>.in-memory.*), diese Pfade können in reference.conf also nicht stehen; sie überschreiben den globalen Block Blatt für Blatt.

nodes.label: Three multi-node suites CI does not run
nodes.norm_label: three multi-node suites ci does not run

nodes.label: Neither multi-node testkit covers wire serialization
nodes.norm_label: neither multi-node testkit covers wire serialization

nodes.label: A budget the per-test timeout cannot reach
nodes.norm_label: a budget the per-test timeout cannot reach

nodes.label: A hang is data, not an abort
nodes.norm_label: a hang is data, not an abort

nodes.label: The harness is checked against known answers
nodes.norm_label: the harness is checked against known answers

nodes.label: Why virtual time beats a wall-clock tolerance
nodes.rationale: Timers fire early as well as late - a 30 ms setTimeout measured as low as 18.7 ms on Bun/Windows and as high as 201 ms under CPU load - so no wall-clock bound is both tight enough to mean something and loose enough to hold, and a more precise clock does not help because the timer is early, not the measurement.
nodes.norm_label: why virtual time beats a wall-clock tolerance

nodes.label: Do not test the framework itself
nodes.norm_label: do not test the framework itself

nodes.label: The timeout is a failure budget
nodes.norm_label: the timeout is a failure budget

nodes.label: Wait on state, not on elapsed time
nodes.norm_label: wait on state, not on elapsed time

nodes.label: When a fixed sleep is still right
nodes.norm_label: when a fixed sleep is still right

nodes.label: ObjectStorageConcurrencyError beim Sweep-CAS
nodes.rationale: Der Sweep schreibt mit Compare-and-Set auf dem ETag; hat die App zuerst geschrieben, bricht er ab - erneut laufen lassen, das frisch geschriebene Objekt ist bereits aktuell.

nodes.label: Snapshot-Key-Layout <prefix>/<persistenceId>/seq-<seqNr>
nodes.rationale: Das Framework listet unter <prefix>/<pid>/, um den neuesten Snapshot zu finden - alle Entity-Typen unter denselben Prefix ohne Per-pid-Unterordner zu packen macht das teuer.

nodes.label: Snapshot-Lifecycle (Save nach Policy, Load per LIST + GET)
nodes.norm_label: snapshot-lifecycle (save nach policy, load per list + get)

nodes.label: Backend-Matrix (Journal / Durable State / Snapshot / Tag-Index)
nodes.rationale: CockroachDB und YugabyteDB sind keine eigenen Backends - sie sprechen das PostgreSQL-Wire-Protokoll. SQLite laeuft auf jeder Runtime, seit der eingebaute node:sqlite-Treiber dazugekommen ist.

nodes.label: CachedSnapshotStoreOptionsType (cache / ttlMs / keyPrefix)
nodes.rationale: keyPrefix (Default 'snap:') verhindert Kollisionen in geteilten Caches.

nodes.label: snapshots-Tabelle, PRIMARY KEY (persistence_id, sequence_nr)
nodes.rationale: Gleiches Pattern wie das Journal; loadLatest liest die hoechste sequence_nr fuer die persistence_id.

nodes.label: Eingebaute Snapshot Stores
nodes.rationale: Journal und Snapshot Store sind unabhaengig und mischbar - z. B. Cassandra-Journal plus Object-Storage-Snapshot-Store.

nodes.label: CachedSnapshotStore
nodes.rationale: A decorator that wraps any SnapshotStore with a TTL read-through cache for loadLatest, backed by any Cache. Worth it only when the underlying store has measurable read latency - slow object storage, expensive decryption, high actor churn, recovery storms; for sub-millisecond SQLite reads it is pure overhead. The underlying store is the constructor's first argument, not an option.

nodes.label: CachedSnapshotStoreOptions
nodes.rationale: cache (required, typically Redis), ttlMs (default 5 minutes) and keyPrefix (default 'snap:') which prevents collisions in shared caches.

nodes.label: withClient(...) to share the journal's connection
nodes.rationale: Passing a pre-built driver client avoids opening a second connection pool.
nodes.norm_label: withclient(...) to share the journal's connection

nodes.label: CassandraSnapshotStore
nodes.rationale: The multi-node snapshot companion to CassandraJournal, shared across cluster nodes. Sharded entities move between nodes, so their snapshot store has to be shared too; a Cassandra journal paired with SQLite snapshots loses the snapshot the moment an entity moves and replays from sequence zero.

nodes.label: CassandraSnapshotStoreOptions
nodes.rationale: The connection fields are the same set the journal takes; snapshotsTable and keepN are the snapshot-specific ones.

nodes.label: save / loadLatest / loadBefore / delete
nodes.rationale: The four SnapshotStore operations, with each persistenceId mapping to an array ordered by sequence number.

nodes.label: keepN retention (SQLite)
nodes.rationale: Maximum snapshots retained per persistenceId, older ones pruned on each save; default 3.

nodes.label: SQLite snapshot performance
nodes.rationale: Write is a single INSERT (~100 us) dominated by serialization rather than SQLite I/O; read is a single sub-millisecond SELECT. For multi-MB state, serialization is the bottleneck.

nodes.label: snapshots SQL table keyed (persistence_id, sequence_nr)
nodes.rationale: Same pattern as the journal; loadLatest reads the highest sequence_nr for a persistence_id.

nodes.label: SqliteSnapshotStoreOptions
nodes.rationale: path, snapshotsTable, keepN, busyTimeoutMs and driver. There is deliberately no `wal` option here, unlike the journal.

nodes.label: SnapshotStore
nodes.rationale: The pluggable store, wired at system creation via withPersistence and independent of the journal - Cassandra journal plus object-storage snapshots is a valid mix. It returns the latest snapshot for a persistenceId on recovery; older ones need the lower-level API.

nodes.label: Passivation (glossary)
nodes.rationale: Stopping an idle sharded entity to free memory; the next message for the same id re-spawns it.

nodes.label: Stability status overview
nodes.rationale: Core actor model, supervision, mailboxes/dispatchers, cluster membership, sharding, singleton, DistributedPubSub, DistributedData, PersistentActor, snapshot stores, migration adapters and broker actors are Stable; replicated event sourcing, worker mesh and Producer/ConsumerController are Experimental.

nodes.label: Journal und Snapshot-Store sind unabhaengig
nodes.rationale: SQLite-Journal + ObjectStorage-Snapshots (lokale Event-Rate, geteilte Snapshots fuer Sharded Entities), Cassandra-Journal + ObjectStorage-Snapshots, oder alles Object Storage - langsamer pro Op, aber billig.

nodes.label: keepN-Pruning (Default 3)
nodes.rationale: Pruning ist standardmaessig aktiv, damit LISTs pro pid beschraenkt bleiben; nur keepN: 0 laesst eine pid unbegrenzt Snapshots ansammeln, sodass jedes loadLatest-LIST alle zurueckgibt.

nodes.label: Indizierte Tag-Query vs. Polling-Scan
nodes.rationale: Beschreibt, was currentEventsByTag in den Storage hinunterdruecken kann: ein Backend mit Tag-Index laeuft ihn ab, die uebrigen scannen das Journal und verfeinern im Speicher - korrekt in beiden Faellen, aber nur mit Index in den Kosten begrenzt.

nodes.label: Geteilter Snapshot-Store über Replicas
nodes.rationale: Jede Replica stellt schneller wieder her, wenn sie den neuesten Snapshot von jeder Replica laden kann, nicht nur ihren eigenen; SqliteSnapshotStore ist für Replicated ES selten sinnvoll.

nodes.label: Der Cache nimmt an, er sei der einzige Writer
nodes.rationale: Schreibt etwas anderes in den zugrunde liegenden Store (manuelles SQL-Update, Batch-Backfill), liefert er veraltete Daten - dann TTL setzen oder manuell invalidieren.
nodes.norm_label: der cache nimmt an, er sei der einzige writer

nodes.label: Backing-Cache (In-Memory / Redis / Memcached)
nodes.rationale: Auf Redis oder Memcached gestuetzt liest jeder Knoten aus demselben Cache, ein auf einem Knoten geladener Snapshot ist auf allen anderen ein Treffer; in-memory behaelt jeder Knoten seine eigene Kopie.

nodes.label: CachedSnapshotStore (Decorator)
nodes.rationale: Nur einsetzen, wenn der zugrunde liegende Store messbare Read-Latenz hat - fuer lokale SQLite-Snapshots fuegt der Cache Overhead ohne Nutzen hinzu. Der zugrunde liegende Store ist das erste Konstruktor-Argument, keine Option.

nodes.label: loadBefore wird nicht gecacht
nodes.rationale: Zu viele moegliche seq-Werte, und selten genutzt - nur bei Recovery.

nodes.label: save = Write-Through mit Invalidierung, kein Write-Back
nodes.rationale: Im Cluster koennen zwei Knoten beim Save konkurrieren; ein lokaler Write-Back wuerde einen veralteten Eintrag hinterlassen. Der naechste Read fuellt neu, und die TTL ist das Sicherheitsnetz, falls ein Knoten zwischen Write und Invalidierung abstuerzt.
nodes.norm_label: save = write-through mit invalidierung, kein write-back

nodes.label: Kompressions- und Verschluesselungs-Optionen werden still ignoriert
nodes.rationale: Anders als die Object-Storage-Stores legt dieser Store den Payload als serialisierten Text ab; entsprechende PersistenceOptions werden stillschweigend ignoriert.
nodes.norm_label: kompressions- und verschluesselungs-optionen werden still ignoriert

nodes.label: keepN pruned beim Speichern, nicht per Timer
nodes.rationale: Eine pid, die nie wieder snapshottet, behaelt was sie hatte - es gibt keinen Hintergrund-Sweep. keepN <= 0 nur mit externer Retention-Policy, sonst waechst die Tabelle unbegrenzt.
nodes.norm_label: keepn pruned beim speichern, nicht per timer

nodes.label: withClient(...) teilt den Driver-Client mit dem Journal
nodes.rationale: Vermeidet zwei Connection-Pools gegen dasselbe Cluster.
nodes.norm_label: withclient(...) teilt den driver-client mit dem journal

nodes.label: Ohne Angabe behaelt er jeden Snapshot
nodes.rationale: Die eine Stelle, an der dieser Store bewusst von der Familie abweicht, in der jeder persistente Store keepN: 3 als Default hat. Weil das der Store ist, den man ohne Konfiguration bekommt, wuerde ein Default-Limit aendern, was jede unkonfigurierte Anwendung aufbewahrt, ohne dass jemand danach gefragt hat.
nodes.norm_label: ohne angabe behaelt er jeden snapshot

nodes.label: Unbegrenztes Wachstum in langen Testlaeufen
nodes.rationale: Ein Benchmark mit 1M Snapshots laesst die Map linear wachsen - keepN setzen, delete selbst aufrufen oder den SQLite-Store mit :memory: verwenden.

nodes.label: busyTimeoutMs (Framework-Default 1000)
nodes.rationale: Die Treiber liefern unterschiedliche Defaults mit (0 ms bei bun:sqlite und node:sqlite, 5000 ms bei better-sqlite3), und das Warten ist synchron, blockiert also die Event-Loop - deshalb setzt das Framework einen eigenen Default.

nodes.label: SQLite-Snapshots brauchen Knoten-Affinitaet
nodes.rationale: Bei Cassandra-Journal geht SQLite fuer Snapshots nur, wenn jede Entity immer auf demselben Node wiederhergestellt wird; fuer Sharded Entities muss auch der Snapshot-Store geteilt sein.

nodes.label: Journal und Snapshot-Store als unabhaengige Dateien
nodes.rationale: Sie koennen auch in dieselbe Datei mit verschiedenen Tabellennamen - aber zwei Dateien halten Operationen einfacher: unabhaengiges Backup, unabhaengiges Vacuum.
nodes.norm_label: journal und snapshot-store als unabhaengige dateien

nodes.label: The cache assumes it is the only writer
nodes.rationale: Anything else writing to the underlying store (a manual SQL update, a batch backfill) makes the cache return stale data - set a TTL or invalidate manually.
nodes.norm_label: the cache assumes it is the only writer

nodes.label: loadBefore is deliberately not cached
nodes.rationale: Too many possible seq values, and it is used rarely - only during recovery.

nodes.label: Sharing the cache across nodes
nodes.rationale: Backed by Redis or Memcached every node reads the same cache, so a snapshot loaded on one node is a hit on all the others; an in-memory cache gives each node its own copy and a fresh node pays the full underlying-load cost.

nodes.label: save is write-through-with-invalidate
nodes.rationale: It delegates then DELETES the cache entry rather than writing the new snapshot back: in a cluster two nodes may race on save, and a local write would leave a stale entry. The next read repopulates, and the TTL is the safety net if a node crashes between the underlying write and the invalidation.

nodes.label: keepN prunes on save, not on a timer
nodes.rationale: Pruning runs inside save, keeping the newest keepN per pid (default 3). A pid that never snapshots again keeps whatever it had - there is no background sweep - so keepN <= 0 only belongs where an external retention policy owns cleanup.
nodes.norm_label: keepn prunes on save, not on a timer

nodes.label: No compression or client-side encryption
nodes.rationale: Unlike the object-storage stores, the payload is stored as serialized text and any PersistenceOptions for compression or encryption are silently ignored - use the object-storage snapshot store when you need either.

nodes.label: snapshots CQL table clustered sequence_nr DESC
nodes.rationale: Descending clustering makes loadLatest a single-row LIMIT 1 read with no scan; loadBefore(seq) just adds a sequence_nr < ? bound. The framework creates the table, not the keyspace (unless autoCreateKeyspace).
nodes.norm_label: snapshots cql table clustered sequence_nr desc

nodes.label: CQL identifier validation
nodes.rationale: keyspace and snapshotsTable are interpolated as identifiers because identifiers cannot be bound, so both are validated against /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/ - including inside the CREATE KEYSPACE autoCreateKeyspace issues. Data-center names are CQL string values instead, so they keep the hyphens an Ec2Snitch name carries and are quote-escaped. Everything else travels as bind parameters.

nodes.label: Unset keepN keeps every snapshot
nodes.rationale: The one place this store deliberately differs from the family, where every persistent store defaults to keepN 3. This is the store you get when nothing is configured, so a default bound would change what every unconfigured application retains without anyone asking for it - opt in explicitly instead.

nodes.label: Re-saving at an existing sequence replaces
nodes.rationale: Rather than appending a second snapshot, matching the relational stores' (persistence_id, sequence_nr) primary key.
nodes.norm_label: re-saving at an existing sequence replaces

nodes.label: busyTimeoutMs has a framework-set default
nodes.rationale: The drivers ship different ones - 0 ms on bun:sqlite and node:sqlite, 5000 ms on better-sqlite3 - and the lock wait is synchronous, so it blocks the event loop. The framework picks one rather than inheriting whichever driver is present.

nodes.label: Journal and snapshot store as independent files
nodes.rationale: They can share one file with different table names, but two files keep operations simpler - back up and vacuum independently.
nodes.norm_label: journal and snapshot store as independent files

nodes.label: Error-handling precedence
nodes.rationale: Three ordered layers: innermost-to-outermost handleErrors (original thrown value, may decline with null), then withErrorHandler (escapees plus backend-internal errors), then the framework default. A handler that throws at step 1 or 2 hands the new error to the next layer.

nodes.label: fallback
nodes.rationale: Answers any request that matched no route, any method. Because it is wired to each backend's not-found hook it must sit at the root of the route tree - a fallback under path() throws at compile time - and there is at most one per server.

nodes.label: handleErrors
nodes.rationale: Scoped error handling: catches anything thrown inside its child (handlers and inner middleware) and sees the original error before any default mapping. Returning null declines and escalates to an outer handler. Nests outside-in like withMiddleware, so the innermost gets first refusal.

nodes.label: HttpError
nodes.rationale: Maps by default to its status plus an {error, ...extra} JSON body, and can carry response headers such as WWW-Authenticate. A thrown HttpError is not logged at error level - it is a response the handler chose, so it stays on the per-request debug line rather than crying wolf.

nodes.label: completeJson
nodes.rationale: The 95% response helper - application/json with the body serialized at write time. complete and completeText cover the raw and text/plain cases.

nodes.label: reject
nodes.rationale: Throws an HttpError with a status, message and extras - the cleanest way to short-circuit a handler. It is typed never, so code after it is dead and TypeScript flags it as unreachable.

nodes.label: Generic 500 redaction
nodes.rationale: The default 500 carries only {error: 'Internal Server Error'} because thrown text routinely holds file paths, SQL fragments, connection strings or a stack, and a 500 is by definition a case nobody wrote a message for. The redaction only works because the detail survives server-side: every escaping throw is logged at error with the error value passed through.

nodes.label: npm minor+patch update group
nodes.rationale: Groups minor and patch bumps into one PR per ecosystem per day rather than 15; major bumps still get their own PR so they can be eyeballed individually.

nodes.label: benchmarks job (typecheck + smoke)
nodes.rationale: typecheck:bench is the stricter check for this failure class — a missing barrel export is a TS2305 even when the binding is never called, whereas Bun elides an unused named import at runtime. bench:smoke then catches wiring that is type-correct but wrong at runtime. `worker` is excluded on hosted runners for the same cause as the multi-node quarantine, and shares its exit criterion.

nodes.label: comparison arms job
nodes.rationale: The comparison tree carries its own package.json and lockfile, so it is invisible to every other job and would be checked by nothing at all — which is exactly how ten benchmark suites sat broken on a removed export for months (#506). Two installs, two manifests; smoke mode writes no result files, since a single unwarmed iteration measures the JIT and letting it reach results/ would replace a committed median with noise.

nodes.label: build job
nodes.rationale: Builds with build:lib (tsc only) since #483. The old build was build:ui && tsc, so it regenerated the very file under test and any check after it passed by construction — using tsc alone removes that hazard structurally instead of relying on step order.

nodes.label: check:ui bundle-currency step
nodes.rationale: The generated bundle is committed on purpose so a fresh clone can typecheck, test and smoke without the UI build — which is exactly what made staleness invisible: the file is valid TypeScript whether or not its contents are current. It compares a source-hash rather than rebuilding and diffing bytes, because gzip stamps the OS into every member and every Bun bump moves the minifier (#521).

nodes.label: docs build job
nodes.rationale: Full-history checkout because Starlight's lastUpdated reads Git history — a shallow checkout makes every page report 'now'. Root dependencies install first so TypeDoc can resolve src/ imports, and Playwright Chromium is fetched separately for Mermaid SSR.

nodes.label: API-drift guard job
nodes.rationale: Doc code fences are never type-checked, so a renamed or removed API silently rots in a snippet until a reader copies it; the guard greps for the names that have bitten us. Pure node:fs/url, so it needs no install step.

nodes.label: docs lockfile-sync job
nodes.rationale: Dependabot bumps docs/package.json but never regenerates docs/bun.lock, and the slow docs build only runs on main at release time — so a drifted lockfile stayed invisible for weeks and then broke the release docs deploy (#473). A ~10 s frozen install fails on the PR instead.

nodes.label: docs deploy job
nodes.rationale: pages: write and id-token: write live in this job rather than at workflow level, so only a one-step job with no checkout and no dependencies can mint the deploy credential; contents: read is deliberately absent because this job never reads the repository.

nodes.label: example frontend build matrix
nodes.rationale: These directories had no CI coverage at all until now, and #890 is the worked example: ts-pattern was declared in all six example package.json files and missing from all six package-lock.json files, so npm ci failed everywhere on develop and nothing noticed. Deliberately `ci`, not `install`: only ci treats a desynced lockfile as an error rather than quietly rewriting it. The matrix is listed explicitly rather than globbed.

nodes.label: example snippets job
nodes.rationale: Until this existed, nothing in CI ever executed an example — a framework change could break every snippet in the tree and the only signal would be a user running one. Bun only, deliberately: the examples are written for Bun, so running them on Node and Deno would test the examples' portability rather than the framework's.

nodes.label: smoke matrix job (bun, bun-floor, node, deno)
nodes.rationale: Bun runs twice — once on the repo pin and once pinned to the engines floor 1.3.0 — so the floor the package claims is actually exercised. Node runs the compiled dist/ deliberately, since that is the surface end-users consume, and the install happens in a Bun-only environment so better-sqlite3 resolves a prebuilt binary instead of a node-gyp source build.
nodes.norm_label: smoke matrix job (bun, bun-floor, node, deno)

nodes.label: bun unit suite job
nodes.rationale: The full bun:test suite runs only under Bun (Bun.serve, better-sqlite3 native compile, fastify autoload). Mirrors test.yml's Bun job without the README-badge side effect, which stays in test.yml as the canonical updater.

nodes.label: quarantined suites job (flag off)
nodes.rationale: Runs exactly the three gated suites with ACTOR_TS_SKIP_FLAKY_MNS deliberately absent; the harness drops it from the child environment by default, so this cannot silently degrade into '3 repeats of 6 skipped tests'. --run-timeout is stated rather than left to the default because the documented symptom is a hang, so the watchdog is what turns tonight into a recorded result instead of a job GitHub killed with nothing to show.

nodes.label: whole-suite stress job
nodes.rationale: Loops the whole suite, quarantined suites included, which is the point: excluding them would report a reliable pass rate over exactly the tests known not to be reliable. A test that failed in EVERY repeat is broken rather than flaky and belongs in an issue, not the flake catalog.

nodes.label: attach-SBOM job
nodes.rationale: Split from the generating job on purpose, not for style: a single job would hold a contents: write credential while running the postinstall scripts of the entire dependency tree, which WorkflowHygiene.test.ts fails on since #622. No checkout and no install here — that is the point of the split. --clobber so the manual re-run fallback does not die on 'asset already exists'.

nodes.label: publish job
nodes.rationale: Typecheck, test and build are deliberately not separate steps: npm publish runs prepublishOnly on the same Bun toolchain immediately before publishing, so explicit steps would run the whole suite twice. The DevTools UI toolchain is installed anyway, because prepublishOnly reaches it and without that the publish would fail at the last possible moment — after the tag and the GitHub Release already exist.

nodes.label: CycloneDX SBOM job
nodes.rationale: --provenance answers who built the tarball and says nothing about what is inside the closure. The install is what makes the SBOM accurate: a bill of materials assembled from unresolved ranges is worse than none, because it looks authoritative and names versions nobody shipped. Ten non-shipping manifests are deleted before the scan, since leaving them in would make the document actively misleading about which advisories affect a release.

nodes.label: npm Trusted Publishing via OIDC
nodes.rationale: No long-lived NPM_TOKEN: the workflow exchanges its short-lived OIDC token for a one-shot publish token at runtime, and --provenance signs via the same id-token. Requires npm >= 11.5.1, which Node 24 already bundles.

nodes.label: README badges job
nodes.rationale: The only job here that can write to the repository and deliberately the only one that runs no third-party code (#622): it installs nothing, builds nothing and re-runs nothing. Runs on !cancelled() rather than success(), because a red suite is exactly when the badge has to flip to red. Values reach the script through env: rather than ${{ }}, since a workflow expression is pasted into the shell before it runs.

nodes.label: Coverage-floor gate step (>= 80%)
nodes.rationale: An unevaluated gate must not read as a passing one, so an unparseable coverage figure fails the step rather than skipping it — unlike the test counts, which only render a badge and must never block a release on a cosmetic parse failure. The 80 floor is pragmatic because the quarantined worker-thread suites remove coverage of machinery that physically cannot execute on a hosted runner.

nodes.label: test job (typecheck + suite with coverage)
nodes.rationale: One run, one source of truth. The suite used to run twice, which gave the parser a different bun output than the one the build status came from — a flaky test under coverage instrumentation could push the badge to '1489 of 1490' while the build stayed green. Read-only and credential-free because this job installs and executes the entire devDependency tree (#622).

nodes.label: typecheck-dev job
nodes.rationale: One tsc --noEmit over tests/, examples/, benchmarks/ and src/ together. It stops the diagnostic count re-inflating: the burn-down that made this green cleared 321 diagnostics, and two of them had arrived in the days before it, from adoption sweeps that missed an example.

nodes.label: One-way batch read and the merge-before-exit fix (#1326)
nodes.rationale: A one-way call completes when the message is dispatched, not when the grain has processed it, so the read could overtake the tail of the batch; the read is now a bounded drain that still times out on dropped messages, so it remains a completion check rather than a way of passing one. Separately, the driver called process.exit(1) before merging, so one arm failing at round 44 discarded eight other arms' hundred rounds.
nodes.norm_label: one-way batch read and the merge-before-exit fix (#1326)

nodes.label: Bun toolchain pinned via .bun-version (#1328)
nodes.rationale: CI read bun-version: latest at 13 of 14 setup-bun sites, so Bun 1.4.0 would have switched every workflow silently, the way 1.3.14 once broke the badge scrape (#1194). A future bump is now a one-line reviewed change that triggers the gates it affects; the supported floor is unchanged, and the nightly quarantine criterion counts nights only while the pin is unchanged (#1330).

nodes.label: Comparison benchmarks run on Linux (#1325)
nodes.rationale: Committed POSIX launchers were recorded at mode 100644, so /bin/sh refused to exec them and every JVM arm died at exit 126. Windows never saw it and no gate did either, because nothing in the repository looked at a file mode; the modes are now asserted against the git INDEX, since the working tree cannot answer that question on Windows — a filesystem check would have passed on the one platform where the bug does not bite. A missing toolchain is now reported as skipped, because a partial run reported as a plain green tick is how a release publishes figures for arms that never ran.

nodes.label: Published comparison figures from a hundred-round Linux run (#1327)
nodes.rationale: Every absolute number moved by a factor of two to five, so the columns are comparable with each other and with nothing quoted before. Three published claims did not survive the move and the pages carry them as corrections rather than restating them quietly — the alternating volley is no longer a tie, and the round-trip row no longer splits by runtime.
nodes.norm_label: published comparison figures from a hundred-round linux run (#1327)

nodes.label: DevTools UI built by Angular 22 instead of Bun.build (#483)
nodes.rationale: A build-time change only. The adapter wraps the shell rather than each panel on purpose: wrapping panels would have meant Angular owning navigation, and with it a shell port smuggled into the issue that was only supposed to change how the bundle is produced. Chunks are attributed to budgets from the builder's metafile rather than file names, since Angular emits chunk-<hash>.js and panel identity survives only in stats.json.
nodes.norm_label: devtools ui built by angular 22 instead of bun.build (#483)

nodes.label: DevTools UI is Angular throughout (#485)
nodes.rationale: withHashLocation() is mandatory rather than stylistic: UiAssetRoutes.ts serves no SPA fallback, so a non-asset path must 404 rather than return the shell, which is what lets one bundle serve at the root and under DevTools.mount('/devtools'). The connection logic was deliberately NOT rewritten — porting it by hand in the same change would have made a regression indistinguishable from a wiring mistake. One defect it found: a computed that mutates during evaluation leaves the view rendering one update behind for ever.

nodes.label: DevTools charts on Apache ECharts (#486)
nodes.rationale: The actor tree stays DOM and the percentage bars stay CSS deliberately — a tree needs search, selection and copyable paths, and a chart engine behind three lines of CSS is pure overhead. Where ECharts has no answer the geometry stayed ours. The 150 to 200 KiB budget move is a measurement, not a preference: ECharts costs 165.9 KB gzip with a single chart type registered, so the old estimate could not have been met by any import set.

nodes.label: DevTools UI test suite (#487)
nodes.rationale: Roughly 3,000 lines had no tests, which was the migration's whole point. The most valuable cover TapClientService against a socket the test drives, because every one of those failure modes is silent in production: a broken refcount leaves the system producing frames for a panel nobody is looking at, and a missed sequence gap renders a tree that quietly disagrees with the real one. Coverage was measured before and after — 93.68% to 93.54% — as the issue asked rather than assumed.

nodes.label: Example frontend bundles no longer committed (#559)
nodes.rationale: 86 tracked files that CI already rebuilds from source. It also retires a question examples.yml documented at length: four of the six builds are not reproducible (Next mints a fresh build id, Svelte stamps a timestamp), so a rebuild-and-diff staleness gate could never have worked — not committing the output dissolves the problem rather than answering it. static/plain and static/lit stay committed because those files are source, not output.
nodes.norm_label: example frontend bundles no longer committed (#559)

nodes.label: formatCount host-dependent grouping fix (#553)
nodes.rationale: Grouping by rewriting the comma out of toLocaleString('en-US') depends on the runtime's ICU data — a comma under Bun, a thin space U+2009 under the Node that runs the UI test suite, where the rewrite therefore hit nothing. Grouped by hand now and pinned by a test that asserts the codepoint rather than the shape.

nodes.label: [Unreleased] window
nodes.rationale: The open window after v0.16.0, dominated by the DevTools UI rebuild (#482 and its parts) and by the comparison-benchmark and toolchain corrections.

nodes.label: Voice sample narrowing and a lifted tsconfig exclude (#1015)
nodes.rationale: Array.prototype.find over a union hands back the whole union, and the casts that reached past it are precisely what stopped the mismatch from being visible where it was written. The tsconfig.dev.json exclusion did not match that file's own stated exclude rule — a file is excluded when a manifest other than the root resolves its imports — and drift is not the only thing a typecheck catches. The gate was checked in both directions before the entry was removed.
nodes.norm_label: voice sample narrowing and a lifted tsconfig exclude (#1015)

nodes.label: Published comparison benchmark tables
nodes.rationale: One machine, one harness, a hundred interleaved rounds, every row verified against work the system actually completed rather than work it was asked for. Presented as ratios, not absolutes, over local in-process message paths only — nothing there says anything about clustering, persistence or a real network.

nodes.label: Chat and voice example applications
nodes.rationale: Two end-to-end sample apps, each with six interchangeable frontends talking the same WebSocket protocol to a clustered backend, exercising sharding, DistributedPubSub, PersistentActor, DistributedData, ClusterSingleton and failover.

nodes.label: src/runtime auto-detecting abstractions
nodes.rationale: TCP sockets, worker threads, SQLite and HTTP serve live behind small abstractions that auto-detect at startup, so the same file runs unchanged under bun run, node and deno run.

nodes.label: Comparison benchmarks against eight arms (#27)
nodes.rationale: benchmarks/comparison/ measures actor-ts against nact, XState, Akka and Pekko through both their Java and Scala APIs, Akka.NET and Orleans, publishing to the README, the bilingual reference/benchmarks pages and a generated RESULTS.md.

nodes.label: Gossip frame sequence field breaks rolling upgrades (#112)
